item.title: Architecture
item.description:
This page describes the design. Where a part is not written yet it says planned.

The pieces 

docker CLI ──► /var/run/docker.sock ──► engine ──► executor ──► a wasip1 module
 (Docker Engine API) │ │
 │ ├─ native: wazero (M1, in progress)
 │ └─ browser worker (planned)
 └─ image store, root filesystem

The engine

A Go program, pure Go, no cgo. It owns the images, the containers and their state, and serves the Docker Engine API. The API reference it is written against is Docker Engine API v1.47; the subset M1 covers is the one the commands pull, run, ps, logs, rm and inspect need: GET /_ping, POST /images/create, the container create, start, list, inspect, logs, wait and delete endpoints. Logs of a container without a TTY use Docker’s multiplexed stream framing.

The Docker CLI

Unchanged. It speaks the Engine API over a Unix socket, /var/run/docker.sock by default, so a learner types the commands they will type on a real host.

The executors

An executor runs one module with a root filesystem, arguments, an environment and a working directory.

  • wazero (M1, in progress): the native executor. wazero is a pure-Go WebAssembly runtime with a WASI preview1 implementation, so the engine stays a single static binary. The container’s root filesystem is adapted to wazero’s writable filesystem interface; the image’s WorkingDir is passed as PWD, which is where a Go wasip1 program takes its initial directory from.
  • Browser worker (planned): the same executor contract implemented over the browser’s WebAssembly, in a Web Worker, so the playground needs no server that runs containers.

The images

An image is an OCI image whose manifest or index entry has os=wasip1 and arch=wasm. The engine pulls from an OCI registry (the Distribution API, with Docker’s bearer-token authentication), selects the wasip1/wasm entry of an index, verifies digests, and unpacks the layers in order — whiteouts included — into the container’s root filesystem. The Wasm OCI artifact layout of the CNCF TAG-Runtime (application/wasm layer, application/vnd.wasm.config.v0+json config) is also read.

Images are meant to be apt-like: a small base plus the tools a lab needs, built from pkgx wasip1 bottles. go-pkgx is gaining a wasip1/wasm target for this; until it ships, images come from whatever registry holds wasip1 images.

What is not in this design yet

Networking (the WasmEdge socket ABI), docker exec and a shell (a WASIX subset), docker build, Compose and a mini-Kubernetes are on the roadmap; none of them exists.
